To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amplitude and velocity of knee joint perturbations influenced the activation of knee joint muscles in different phases of the reflex response.
stimulus amplitude influenced reflex responses during P1, and stimulus velocity influenced reflex responses during impulse (P2).
the reflex responses of knee joint muscles are differentially affected by stimulus characteristics during sudden perturbations of the knee joint.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether the stretch reflex of knee joint muscles is modulated by stimulus characteristics.
the question whether stimulus characteristics influence specific reflex components of the knee joint.
the effects of different stimulus characteristics on the reflex activation of knee joint muscles during a sudden perturbation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stretch reflex is not a simple reflex but rather a complex interaction of several reflex components.
the reflex responses are a combination of afferent input from the muscle, joint and skin.
the influence of the stimulus characteristics on the reflex response depends on the specific muscle and the specific timeframe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reflex responses of the quadriceps are mainly determined by the stretch velocity, whereas the amplitude of the stimulus is more important for the hamstring muscles.
the reflex activation of muscles of the knee joint depends on the stimulus characteristics of the applied perturbation.
the influence of stimulus characteristics on muscle activation depends on muscle and time frame.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stretch reflex is a complex phenomenon and its components should be investigated separately.
reflex responses are not only influenced by the stimulus amplitude, but also by the rate of force development.
the reflex responses of the knee joint are more complex than previously thought.
